body:
> Prerequisite named by the /kanban:groom design (#191). Today `hkb link` takes exactly one parent and one child, so a groom plan that files a card under two parents, or re-links three children to a survivor, is three commands and three writes.

## What

- `hkb link <parent> <child>...` accepts many children; `hkb link --blocked-by a,b <child>` accepts many parents; one board read, one write per edge, one line per edge in the output, `--json` returns the edges written and the ones that already existed.
- `hkb unlink` mirrors it.

## Done when

- `hkb link 155 116 130` writes two dependencies and prints two lines; re-running prints "already linked" and writes nothing. Tests in test/lifecycle.test.js. `npm run lint && npm test` green.
goal: Linking a card under several parents, or several children under one parent, is one command with one board read
title: hkb link takes several children at once: hkb link <parent> <child>... and hkb create --blocked-by a,b already exist — make the bulk form the default
